entries.subject: Radius
entries.finding: 1.18 Jupiter radii from the NASA Exoplanet Archive's calculated radius (its Chen & Kipping 2017 mass-radius relationship): a model, not a measurement, since HD 73344 d does not transit, via the NASA Exoplanet Archive.

entries.subject: Mass
entries.finding: 2.55 Jupiter masses: Zhang et al. 2025, the mass the NASA Exoplanet Archive's composite table adopts (2025AJ....169..200Z), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....169..200Z/abstract).

entries.subject: Orbit
entries.finding: Zhang et al. 2025 (2025AJ....169..200Z), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname ZHANG_ET_AL_2025): P 5823 d; Zhang et al. 2025 (2025AJ....169..200Z), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname ZHANG_ET_AL_2025): a/R* derived from its semi-major axis 6.7 au and stellar radius 1.22 solar radii; inclination 59 +19 degrees, measured in the same fit; Zhang et al. 2025 (2025AJ....169..200Z), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname ZHANG_ET_AL_2025): e 0.18; Zhang et al. 2025 (2025AJ....169..200Z), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname ZHANG_ET_AL_2025): omega 58.9 degrees; Zhang et al. 2025 (2025AJ....169..200Z), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname ZHANG_ET_AL_2025): periastron passage 2458061 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; Display convention: the NASA Exoplanet Archive carries no position angle for the orbit's node on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north)..
